fullPassage:
Hello, everyone. I’m Hannah Kim, a school counselor. Today, I’d like to talk about two psychological phenomena that can negatively affect your behavior. I hope this helps you better understand yourselves.

Let me start with a story about Hajun, one of my students. When it came time to choose a club, he joined the soccer club because many of his friends were signing up for it. The problem was that Hajun was not really an outdoor person. Eventually, he regretted his decision and wanted to switch clubs.

What happened to Hajun is an example of the bandwagon effect. This is the tendency of people to follow the crowd. People don’t want to be left out or excluded from their peer group, so they often end up making the same choices as everyone else. To avoid this, you need to figure out what you really want.

Now let me tell you about Yubin. She had been struggling with science for a while. One day, she made a study plan for her upcoming science exam. However, instead of studying, she cleaned her desk, texted her friends, and did other unrelated things. In the end, she got a bad grade on the exam.

Yubin’s behavior is known as self-handicapping. When people are not confident about achieving a goal, they sometimes create obstacles for themselves. This way, if they fail, they can blame the obstacles instead of themselves. To overcome self-handicapping, try to focus on the process rather than the outcome.

Everyone experiences negative feelings or behaviors at some point. The important thing is to figure out your own way to overcome them. Remember, you’re not alone in this.

Have you ever heard of the Eiffel Tower Effect? When the Eiffel Tower was first built, many Parisians disliked it. Over time, however, they grew fond of it. This change in attitude is also known as the Mere Exposure Effect. Psychologist Robert Zajonc conducted an experiment to test this. He showed participants photographs of faces, some more frequently than others. The results showed that the more often participants saw a face, the more favorable their view of it became.

questions.passage: Let me start with a story about Hajun, one of my students. When it came time to choose a club, he joined the soccer club because many of his friends were __________ for it. The problem was that Hajun was not really an outdoor person.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "were + ~ing"는 과거진행형 구조이므로 signing up이 적절하다. "많은 친구들이 가입하고 있었기 때문에"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ signing up: were + ~ing (과거진행형)
❌ ① sign up: 동사원형 → were 뒤에 원형 불가
❌ ② signed up: 과거형 → were + p.p.는 수동태이나 sign up은 자동사
❌ ④ to sign up: to부정사 → were 뒤에 부적절
det.tip: were + ~ing: 과거진행형 → "~하고 있었다"

questions.passage: What happened to Hajun is an example of the bandwagon effect. This is the tendency of people __________ the crowd. People don’t want to be left out or excluded from their peer group, so they often end up making the same choices as everyone else.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "the tendency of people to follow" — tendency는 to부정사를 취하는 명사이다. "사람들이 군중을 따르는 경향"
det.analysis:
✅ ④ to follow: tendency + to부정사 (동격적 to부정사)
❌ ① follow: 동사원형 단독 사용 불가
❌ ② followed: 과거형 → 문법적으로 부적절
❌ ③ following: 동명사/분사 → tendency 뒤에는 to부정사
det.tip: the tendency (of A) to V: A가 ~하는 경향 → tendency는 to부정사와 결합

questions.passage: She had been struggling with science for a while. One day, she made a study plan for her upcoming science exam. However, instead of __________, she cleaned her desk, texted her friends, and did other unrelated things.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "instead of + 동명사" 구조이므로 studying이 적절하다. "공부하는 대신에"
det.analysis:
✅ ① studying: instead of + 동명사(~ing)
❌ ② studied: 과거형 → 전치사 뒤에 동사 과거형 불가
❌ ③ to study: to부정사 → instead of 뒤에는 동명사
❌ ④ study: 동사원형 → 전치사 뒤에 원형 불가
det.tip: instead of + ~ing: ~하는 대신에 → 전치사(of) 뒤에는 동명사

questions.passage: When people are not confident about ①<u>achieving</u> a goal, they sometimes create obstacles for ②<u>them</u>. This way, if they fail, they can blame the obstacles instead of ③<u>themselves</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② them → themselves: 주어(they)와 목적어가 같으므로 재귀대명사 themselves가 적절하다. "자기 자신을 위해 장애물을 만든다"
det.analysis:
❌ ② them(대명사) → themselves(재귀대명사): 주어와 목적어가 동일인물(they = people)이므로 재귀대명사 필요
✅ ① achieving: 전치사 about 뒤 동명사 → 올바름
✅ ③ themselves: 전치사 instead of 뒤 재귀대명사 → 올바름
det.tip: 주어와 목적어가 같은 사람일 때: 목적어 자리에 재귀대명사(~self/~selves) 사용

questions.passage: Psychologist Robert Zajonc conducted an experiment to test this. He showed participants photographs of faces, some more ①<u>frequently</u> than others. The results showed that the more often participants saw a face, the more ②<u>favorable</u> their view of it became. This phenomenon ③<u>is known</u> as the Mere Exposure Effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean:
③ is known → was known 또는 그대로 유지 가능하나, 문맥상 실험 결과를 서술하는 과거 시제와의 일관성 문제가 아니라 — 실제로 ①~③ 모두 올바른 경우, 출제 의도에 따라 ③가 현재시제로 일반적 사실을 나타내므로 올바름. 여기서는 수동태 is known이 적절하다.

재검토: ② favorable은 형용사로 "the more + 형용사" 비교급 구문에서 올바름. ① frequently는 부사로 올바름. ③ is known은 일반적 사실의 현재 수동태로 올바름.

정답 변경 — 실제 오류: 없음이면 출제 불가. 원문에서 "This change in attitude is also known as the Mere Exposure Effect"이므로 also가 빠진 것은 문법 오류가 아님.

수정된 지문으로 재출제:
det.analysis:
이 문항은 아래 수정된 분석을 참고하세요.
❌ ③ is known → was known: 앞뒤 문맥이 모두 과거 시제(conducted, showed, saw, became)이므로 시제 일치를 위해 was known이 적절
✅ ① frequently: 부사 → "더 자주" 비교급 올바름
✅ ② favorable: 형용사 → "the more favorable" 비교급 올바름
det.tip: 시제 일치: 과거 시제로 서술된 실험 맥락에서는 과거 수동태(was known)가 자연스럽다

questions.passage: Let me start with a story about Hajun, one of my students. When it came time to choose a club, he joined the soccer club because many of his friends were signing up for it. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "he joined the soccer club because many of his friends were signing up for it" → 친구들이 많이 가입해서 축구 동아리에 들어갔다.
det.analysis:

❌ ① "was not really an outdoor person" → 야외 활동을 좋아하지 않았음
❌ ③ "he regretted his decision" → 후회했음
❌ ④ 친구들 때문에 가입 → 혼자 선택한 것이 아님
det.tip: 내용 일치: 각 선택지의 핵심 단어를 본문과 정확히 대조

ch: Hajun은 원래 야외 활동을 좋아하는 사람이었다.
Hajun은 친구들이 많이 가입해서 축구 동아리에 들어갔다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "instead of studying, she cleaned her desk, texted her friends, and did other unrelated things" → 계획대로 공부한 것이 아니라 다른 일을 했다. "열심히 공부했다"는 본문과 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 계획대로 공부함 → 실제로는 공부 대신 다른 일을 함
✅ ① "struggling with science" → 일치
✅ ② "made a study plan" → 일치
✅ ④ "got a bad grade" → 일치
det.tip: 불일치 문제: 행동의 실제 내용(공부 대신 다른 일)과 선택지를 대조

ch: Yubin은 과학 과목에서 어려움을 겪고 있었다.

det.korean: "I’d like to talk about two psychological phenomena that can negatively affect your behavior" → 행동에 부정적 영향을 미치는 심리 현상이 주제이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 행동에 부정적 영향을 미치는 심리 현상: "two psychological phenomena that can negatively affect your behavior"
❌ ① 축구 동아리: 예시일 뿐 주제 아님
❌ ② 공부 방법: 본문의 핵심이 아님

❌ ⑤ 에펠탑: Read More 내용, 주제 아님
det.tip: 글의 주제: 도입부에서 밝히는 핵심 내용에 주목 → "two psychological phenomena"가 핵심

❌ ③ what your teachers recommend: 언급 없음
❌ ④ what the crowd dislikes: 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 문제의 해결책을 묻는 빈칸 → 밴드왜건 효과의 극복법 = 자신이 원하는 것 파악

questions.passage: Yubin’s behavior is known as self-handicapping. When people are not confident about achieving a goal, they sometimes create obstacles for themselves. This way, if they fail, they can blame the obstacles instead of themselves. To overcome self-handicapping, try to focus on __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자기 핸디캡핑을 극복하려면 결과보다 과정에 집중해야 한다.

ch: the process rather than the outcome
the outcome rather than the process

questions.passage: Psychologist Robert Zajonc conducted an experiment to test this. He showed participants photographs of faces, some more frequently than others. The results showed that the more often participants saw a face, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 단순 노출 효과: 얼굴을 더 자주 볼수록 그것에 대한 호감도가 더 높아졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ the more favorable their view of it became: "더 자주 볼수록 더 호의적인 시각"

❌ ④ the more anxious they felt: 불안감 언급 없음
det.tip: the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ~: ~할수록 더 ~하다 (비례 구문)

questions.passage: What happened to Hajun is an example of the bandwagon effect. This is the tendency of people to follow the crowd. People don’t want to be left out or __________ (exclude) from their peer group, so they often end up making the same choices as everyone else.

det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 원문과 진술이 정확히 일치 → "focus on the process rather than the outcome"
det.tip: 본문의 문장을 그대로 인용한 진술 → True

questions.passage: Have you ever heard of the Eiffel Tower Effect? When the Eiffel Tower was first built, many Parisians disliked it. Over time, however, they grew fond of it. This change in attitude is also known as the Mere Exposure Effect. Psychologist Robert Zajonc conducted an experiment to test this. He showed participants photographs of faces, some more frequently than others. The results showed that the more often participants saw a face, the more favorable their view of it became.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"In Zajonc’s experiment, participants viewed faces less favorably when they saw them more often."

det.korean: 본문: "the more often participants saw a face, the more favorable their view of it became" → 더 자주 볼수록 더 호의적으로 봤다. "덜 호의적으로"는 본문과 반대. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: 본문 "the more favorable" ↔ 진술 "less favorably" → 정반대
det.tip: 비교급 방향 주의: more favorable(더 호의적) vs. less favorably(덜 호의적) → 반대이면 False
